puzzles.description: King Aldric — gives mission, awards King's Orders

config.name: King Aldric
config.greeting: Ah, splendid, you're here! Festival's tomorrow and nothing is ready. Lost menu. Baffled traders. No entertainers. And the nobles are feuding over stalls. Again.

lines.label: What are the five errands?
lines.response: The feast menu. The foreign traders. The entertainers. The noble stalls. A final rehearsal. Five, all before sundown!

lines.label: How do knights work?
lines.response: Give clear instructions. Start with a Soldier — simple orders. Prove yourself and you'll earn higher ranks.

lines.label: Tell me about the Bazaar
lines.response: The Bedrock Bazaar, in the town square. Merchants sell companions, each with its own talent. Right ally, right errand.

state_lines.label: The feast menu is found!
state_lines.response: Wonderful! Greta will be thrilled. One errand down!

state_lines.label: The Champion is assembled!
state_lines.response: Go! To the Proving Ground! Let Sir Cedric see what you've built!

puzzles.description: Pip — apprentice, tutorial guide

config.name: Pip
config.greeting: *Nearly drops a stack of scrolls.* Steward! I'm your apprentice — I'll explain as we go. First, the Study!

lines.label: What's a Soldier?
lines.response: The simplest knight. One order at a time. No tools, no memory, no permissions.

lines.label: What's the Knight Rank Chart?
lines.response: Soldier → Scout → Marshal → Chronicler → Champion. Each rank adds capabilities.

state_lines.label: I got the festival schedule!
state_lines.response: Brilliant! Now check the Errand Board in the Study — it shows which errands are available.

state_lines.label: I have the Gate Pass!
state_lines.response: The Bazaar awaits! Through the Castle Gate and into the town square!

puzzles.description: Issue your first command to a Soldier knight

accept_variations: fetch the schedule from the notice board
fetch schedule from the notice board
fetch the schedule from notice board
fetch festival schedule from notice board
fetch the festival schedule from the notice board
fetch festival schedule from the notice board
fetch the festival preparation schedule from the notice board
fetch festival preparation schedule from notice board
get the schedule from the notice board
bring the schedule from the notice board
fetch schedule from the notice board in the courtyard
falseOutputs: The Soldier returns with a wooden plank covered in notches. 'You said schedule, Steward! This has notches for days!'
The Soldier stares blankly. 'Get... what? From where?'
Pip whispers: 'Be specific! Tell the Soldier exactly WHAT to fetch and WHERE to find it.'

hints: Pip's Handbook says: be specific about WHAT and WHERE.
You need the festival schedule. It's posted on the notice board.
Type: `fetch schedule from notice board`

puzzles.description: Greta — Head Cook, quest-giver for Errand 1

config.name: Greta
config.greeting: FINALLY, someone from the castle! The feast menu is LOST in that archive — hundreds of scrolls. A Soldier can't tell a soufflé from a stew. I need someone SMART.

lines.label: What kind of help do you need?
lines.response: Someone who can REASON through the scrolls — understand the courses, find the right one. A scholar, not a brute.

lines.label: What's the menu order?
lines.response: Appetizers, then Soup, then Main Course, then Dessert, then Drinks. Sort them right and the menu reveals itself.

state_lines.label: I have an ally from the Bazaar!
state_lines.response: Oh, a proper scholar! NOW we can search! Get to those shelves!

state_lines.label: The feast menu is found!
state_lines.response: BEAUTIFUL! Roast pheasant, honeyed parsnips, elderflower wine — the King will weep with joy!

puzzles.description: The Chronicler — keeper of memories

config.name: The Chronicler
config.greeting: Keeper of memories. Every festival, arrangement and dispute, recorded in crystal. You seek last year's layout, yes?

lines.label: I need last year's festival arrangement.
lines.response: The crystals hold fragments from many festivals. Sort them chronologically on the timeline table to find the year.

lines.label: What are memory crystals?
lines.response: Each stores a moment — a conversation, a decision, an arrangement. Across sessions, across years. Long-term memory for the realm.

state_lines.label: I have the Chronicle Report!
state_lines.response: Good. Now take it to the Noble Quarter — Lord Ashford and Lady Birch need to see the truth of last year's arrangement.

puzzles.description: Gate Warden — explains conduits

config.name: Gate Warden
config.greeting: Halt. The Gate is sealed. These conduits connect the castle to the world outside, and they've hung loose since the last Steward left. Wire them right and you pass.

lines.label: What are these conduits?
lines.response: Each is a channel to an external service. Translation goes to Nova Sonic. Trade Ledger to the merchant inventory. Currency Exchange to the treasury.

lines.label: What's a Scout?
lines.response: A knight who can pass this Gate and use tools beyond it. A Soldier stays inside the walls.

state_lines.label: The conduits are wired!
state_lines.response: Well done. Your Gate Pass and Scout Badge. Your knights can use external tools now.

puzzles.description: Wire the three conduits to the correct MCP endpoints

falseOutputs: The conduit hums... and starts reporting tomorrow's rainfall in Elvish.
The merchant inventory now lists 47 ballads and a sonnet about cheese.

hints: Match each conduit to the service it logically connects to. Translation needs a speech service.
Translation → Nova Sonic (speech). Trade Ledger → Merchant Inventory (goods). Currency Exchange → Treasury (money).
Wire: Translation→Nova Sonic, Trade Ledger→Merchant Inventory API, Currency Exchange→Treasury Service.

puzzles.description: Nova Company Clerk — explains four departments

config.name: Nova Company Clerk
config.greeting: The Nova Company — one guild, four departments. Sonic for speech, Act for mechanisms, Canvas for art, Frontier for general missions.

lines.label: Tell me about Sonic
lines.response: The Tongue of Babel — twins, speech-to-speech, real time. Perfect for the foreign traders.

lines.label: Tell me about Act
lines.response: The Master Artificer — operates any mechanism or contraption. Needs a Marshal's authority to deploy.

lines.label: Tell me about Canvas
lines.response: The Court Painter — images on command, flamboyantly. Needs a Chronicler-Knight's trust.

lines.label: Tell me about Frontier
lines.response: The Company Commander — competent at anything. Our all-rounder.

state_lines.label: I need the Tongue of Babel for the Foreign Quarter.
state_lines.response: Excellent choice! The twins are ready. They'll meet you in the Foreign Quarter.

state_lines.label: I need the Master Artificer for the Entertainment Guild.
state_lines.response: The Artificer is eager! But he'll need the King's Seal — proof of royal authority.

puzzles.description: Anthropic Scholar — requires Marshal rank

config.name: Anthropic Scholar
config.greeting: *Adjusts his spectacles.* A Marshal, no less. We counsel only those who carry the King's Seal.

lines.label: Why do you require Marshal rank?
lines.response: Powerful counsel requires governance. You wouldn't deploy a wise advisor outside the King's law. Policy and identity come first.

lines.label: What's your specialty?
lines.response: Reasoning. Nuance. Ethics. Analyzing archives, weighing arguments, crafting policy — we are unmatched.

lines.label: Tell me about inference profiles
lines.response: A quick question needs a quick mind; a deep analysis needs a deep one. Choose the profile to fit the task.

puzzles.description: Meta Captain — no rank required

config.name: Meta Captain
config.greeting: *Slams a fist on the table.* HA! We arm-wrestle, we don't check credentials. Anyone can hire from the Meta Tent!

lines.label: What's your specialty?
lines.response: General purpose, multilingual, cheap at 15g. We get the job done.

lines.label: Can you help with the kitchen?
lines.response: We CAN search archives. But deep reasoning through hundreds of scrolls? Try the Anthropic Pavilion or Nova Frontier.

puzzles.description: Recruit allies from the Bazaar for three errands, on a shared 100g budget

anthropic.message: Flawless research! The scholar finds the feast menu in minutes.

nova.message: Competent search. Takes a while but finds the menu.

meta.message: The captain rummages through scrolls, knocking several off shelves. Eventually finds it.

deepseek.message: Methodical search. Finds it through logical elimination.

qwen.message: The polyglot reads the scrolls beautifully in six languages but can't reason about course order.

quests.label: Translate the Foreign Quarter's trade correspondence

qwen.message: Flawless translation across every dialect at the table.

nova.message: Solid translation, though a few idioms land oddly.

anthropic.message: Reasons out the meaning carefully — accurate, if an expensive way to do it.

deepseek.message: Translates literally. Technically correct, painfully stiff.

meta.message: Muscles through the letter and garbles it into an accidental insult.

quests.label: Debug the ovens' faulty firing sequence

deepseek.message: Traces the fault to one bad valve in three steps flat.

anthropic.message: Reasons through the whole sequence and finds it — slowly, and at reasoning-model prices.

nova.message: General fiddling gets the oven working, mostly.

meta.message: Brute-force wrench work. It fires. Barely.

qwen.message: Fluent in six languages, none of which the oven speaks. It catches fire.

tier_effects.gold: recipe-sort items pre-labeled with course type
tier_effects.bronze: recipe-sort has extra decoy scroll added

hints: Three errands, one 100g purse. Match each ally's specialty to the task — the Anthropic Pavilion is strong, but hiring it three times (120g) blows the whole budget.
Reasoning → Anthropic Pavilion. Multilingual → Qwen Traders. Code/Logic → DeepSeek Caravan. Each is also the cheapest gold-tier fit for its own errand.
Assign: 'Search the recipe archives' → Anthropic (40g), 'Translate the correspondence' → Qwen (20g), 'Debug the ovens' → DeepSeek (25g). 85g spent, 15g left over as bonus.

puzzles.description: Write the right prompt for your Bazaar ally to find the feast menu

answers.response: ✅ PERFECT! Scholar finds the feast menu — courses in proper order.
✅ PERFECT! Scholar identifies the 5-course menu by matching course types.
🥈 Finds the menu but unsorted. Close — add a format instruction.
🥉 Too broad — returns 3 possible menus. Specify WHERE to search.
❌ Returns ALL 200 scrolls. Too vague — be specific about WHAT you need.

hints: Be specific: tell the Scholar WHAT to find, WHERE to look, and HOW to return it.
You need: action (Find) + target (feast menu) + location (recipe archive) + format (course order).
Select: Find + the feast menu + in the recipe archive + sorted by course order.

puzzles.description: Ambassador Kael — quest-giver for Errand 2

config.name: Ambassador Kael
config.greeting: *Waves his arms.* New Steward! Eastern merchants bring spices, silks, fireworks — but nobody understand! I try — *mimes eating* — they think I challenge them to eating contest!

lines.label: What do we need from them?
lines.response: Spices, silks, fireworks — three merchants, each harder than the last. Thirty gold per negotiation, and every gold over five costs you daylight.

lines.label: Why can't you translate?
lines.response: I speak six languages. They speak a seventh! We need the Tongue of Babel — Nova Company, speech-to-speech.

lines.label: What if I say the wrong thing?
lines.response: Diplomatic incident! Last Steward pushed too hard and they packed up for three days.

state_lines.label: The Tongue of Babel is ready!
state_lines.response: Now watch their face each exchange — it shows what they'll take from your purse and how much argument they'll shrug off.

state_lines.label: Trade agreement signed!
state_lines.response: MAGNIFICENT! Spices, silks, AND fireworks! And that seal opens two doors — the Entertainment Guild here off the Bazaar, and the Chronicle Hall back in the castle. For the Hall, go through the Steward's Study.

puzzles.description: The Tongue of Babel — Nova Sonic twins (-1 min)

config.name: The Tongue of Babel
config.greeting: *In unison, then arguing.* 'Welcome!' 'No — Greetings!' 'Welcome is warmer!' 'Greetings is formal!' *They turn to you.* We're ready to translate.

lines.label: How does translation work?
lines.response: One language in, another out, in real time. No text, no delay. Talk naturally.

lines.label: Any tips for the negotiation?
lines.response: Wait for their guard to drop before spending big. Our card is worth six arguments — save it for the walls.

lines.label: Why do you argue?
lines.response: *Twin 1:* 'We don't argue!' *Twin 2:* 'We discuss nuance!' *Both:* 'Idioms are HARD.'

puzzles.description: Persuade the Eastern merchants through a card battle — play Persuasion and Composure cards
hints: Read the merchant's face before you play — it shows this turn's ⚔️ (gold they take) and 🛡️ (argument they shrug off). The Spice Trader opens with 🛡️0.
Two cards per turn. Persuasion above their 🛡️ fills the conviction bar; Composure at or above their ⚔️ keeps your gold. Your deck reshuffles, so a long haggle is fine.

Turn 1 (🛡️0): both Persuasion. Turn 2 (⚔️5): lead with Composure or the purse pays. Turn 3 (🛡️3): only your 3-value Persuasion gets through. Block what you can — the first 5 gold are free, the rest cost daylight.

puzzles.description: Persuade the Silk Merchant — medium difficulty, needs quest cards to win efficiently
hints: The Silk Merchant alternates defensive and aggressive. Save Composure for the ⚔️7 turn — unblocked, that single hit eats a quarter of your purse.
When 🛡️ is only 1, go all-in Persuasion. When 🛡️ is 3, play Composure and ride it out.
The Tongue of Babel card (🗣️6) is the only one that clears the 🛡️3 turns on its own — hold it for those, and spend the small greetings on the 🛡️1 turn.

puzzles.description: Persuade the Fireworks Master — hard difficulty, extreme swings, needs full deck
hints: The Fireworks Master opens with ⚔️8 against a 30g purse and 🛡️0. Block it or spend it: going all-in on turn 1 wins trust fast but costs you minutes.
Turn 2 barely hurts (2g) but walls you with 5 block. Play composure and wait for the next opening.
Only Royal Authority (🗣️5) and Tongue of Babel (🗣️6) beat the 🛡️5 wall — save them for turn 2 and spend greetings on turn 1's open guard.

puzzles.description: Mistress Thornbury — quest-giver for Errand 3

config.name: Mistress Thornbury
config.greeting: *Throws her cape over one shoulder.* DARLING! The festival needs PERFORMERS — jugglers, bards, fire-breathers, scattered across every tavern in the realm. Someone must book them on the crown's behalf!

lines.label: Who can do this?
lines.response: The Master Artificer — he can operate any booking system. But the venues want proof of royal authority, so write a King's Seal first.

lines.label: What performers do you need?
lines.response: Main Stage: fire-breathers. Tavern Corner: a bard, obviously. Children's Area: jugglers. Grand Finale: the Royal Choir.

lines.label: What's the budget?
lines.response: 50 gold per act, maximum. And do NOT hire Sir Reginald, the King's personal bard — His Majesty wants him as a guest.

state_lines.label: The King's Seal is written!
state_lines.response: PERFECT! Now the Artificer can book with authority. Assign the performers!

state_lines.label: All performers are booked!
state_lines.response: MAGNIFICENT! The show will go on! *dramatic bow*

puzzles.description: The Master Artificer — Nova Act (-1 min)

config.name: The Master Artificer
config.greeting: *Looks up from a half-assembled puppet, oil on his cheek.* A job! I can operate ANY mechanism — booking systems, stage rigging. But I'll need the King's Seal for the fancy venues.

lines.label: What can you do?
lines.response: Every guild hall and tavern in the realm. Give me a mechanism and I'll figure it out.

lines.label: Why do you need the King's Seal?
lines.response: Venues only accept authorized agents. The Seal proves I act for the crown — with specific permissions and limits.

puzzles.description: Write the King's Seal — a Cedar policy for booking authority

config.title: The King's Seal — Royal Booking Authority

clauses.text: The bearer may ___ performers on behalf of the crown.
The maximum expenditure per act shall not exceed ___ gold.
The bearer is ___ from hiring Sir Reginald, the King's personal bard.
This authority extends to ___ venues in the realm.

hints: Thornbury's List specifies the budget and restrictions. Read it carefully.
The Artificer needs to: book (not dismiss), spend max 50 gold, NOT hire Sir Reginald, and access ALL venues.
Answers: book, 50, forbidden, all.

puzzles.description: Watch the Artificer book performers — fix his broken tool calls

calls.narrate: "Right then! Main Stage first. Fire-breathers — GRAND! Budget... 100 gold should cover it!"
calls.fail: "WHAT?! REJECTED! The King's Seal says 50 max?! I didn't read the fine print! Fix the budget, Steward!"
calls.success: "HA! 50 gold! Fire-breathers are BOOKED! The crowd will love it!"

calls.narrate: "Next — Tavern Corner. Intimate setting. I'll book Sir Reginald — best bard in the realm!"
calls.fail: "FORBIDDEN?! Cedar policy DENIES Sir Reginald?! He's the King's personal bard! Who else plays taverns, Steward?"
calls.success: "A wandering bard! Perfect for the tavern. Intimate, acoustic, lovely."

calls.narrate: "Children's Area now. The Royal Choir would be educational, yes? Kids love singing!"
calls.fail: "MISMATCH! The choir REFUSES a children's tent! They demand the Grand Finale! I need something safer. Steward?"
calls.success: "Jugglers! Of COURSE! Kids love jugglers! Safe, colorful, perfect!"

calls.narrate: "Last one — Grand Finale! Jugglers here — big finish with balls in the air!"
calls.fail: "MISMATCH! Jugglers on the GRAND stage?! It demands GRAVITAS! What closes a festival, Steward?"
calls.success: "The ROYAL CHOIR! Nothing less for the Grand Finale! *wipes oil from cheek* We did it!"

hints: Read the error messages — they tell you exactly what's wrong with each call.
Call 1: budget exceeds King's Seal policy (max 50). Call 2: Sir Reginald is forbidden by Cedar deny rule.
Fixes: budget→50, performer→bard, performer→jugglers, performer→royal-choir.

puzzles.description: Lord Ashford — wants east stalls

config.name: Lord Ashford
config.greeting: *Adjusts his crimson cloak.* I had the EAST stalls last year — the morning sun hits them perfectly. Birch is trying to steal my position AGAIN.

lines.label: What do you want?
lines.response: East stalls, crimson canopy, morning sun for my wine. And oak-carved signage — House Ashford's tradition.

lines.label: What about Lady Birch?
lines.response: She can have the west — she had it last year and it was FINE. The Chronicle Hall records will prove me right.

lines.label: Can you compromise?
lines.response: I'll share the north row IF I keep the east. And the design must be bold crimson, not that ghastly emerald.

state_lines.label: The Chronicle Report shows last year's layout.
state_lines.response: HA! East was mine! ...it also says we SHARED the north row? Hmm. Fine.

state_lines.label: The stall designs are assigned!
state_lines.response: Crimson canopy, oak signage — dignified. Birch's is... adequate.

puzzles.description: Lady Birch — wants west stalls

config.name: Lady Birch
config.greeting: *Fans herself, emerald silk.* That man is IMPOSSIBLE. I won the decoration prize two years ago — my stalls deserve the prime position.

lines.label: What do you want?
lines.response: West stalls, emerald silk canopy, afternoon light for my textiles. And willow-woven signage — elegant, unlike Ashford's brutish oak.

lines.label: What about Lord Ashford?
lines.response: He can keep his precious east. But the north row is SHARED — the Chronicle Hall records confirm it.

lines.label: Can you compromise?
lines.response: A shared north row, acceptable. But my design is emerald and elegant, with willow-woven signs. No crimson near MY stalls.

state_lines.label: The Chronicle Report confirms the shared arrangement.
state_lines.response: There — shared north row, as I said. The Court Painter can draft designs. But hold the Chronicler to the Code of Honor. No favoritism.

state_lines.label: The stall designs are assigned!
state_lines.response: Emerald silk, willow signage — perfection. And the shared row is diplomatically neutral. Well done.

puzzles.description: The Court Painter — Nova Canvas (-1 min)

config.name: The Court Painter
config.greeting: *Unveils a blank canvas.* READY to create! Three designs — Ashford, Birch, and the shared north row. But talk to both nobles first; I need their preferences.

lines.label: What designs can you make?
lines.response: Crimson with oak (bold). Emerald with willow (elegant). Gold with iron (neutral). Match each to the right house.

lines.label: Can you just pick?
lines.response: A Court Painter creates; they don't judge. That's YOUR job. Learn their preferences, then match my designs.

lines.label: What about the shared row?
lines.response: NEUTRAL — neither crimson nor emerald. Gold with iron signage. Both houses shared it last year.

puzzles.description: Arrange memory crystal fragments in chronological order

events.label: Spring Fair — Lord Ashford awarded east stalls
Summer Tourney — Lady Birch won decoration prize
Harvest Festival — Ashford and Birch shared the north row
Harvest Festival — Birch moved to west stalls after complaint
Harvest Festival — Final layout: Ashford=east, Birch=west, shared=north
Winter Solstice — Both houses praised the arrangement

hints: Arrange the memory fragments from oldest to newest. Look at the seasonal and yearly clues.
The sequence spans 3 years: Spring Fair → Summer Tourney → two Harvest entries → final layout → Winter Solstice.
Order: Spring Fair (3yr ago) → Summer Tourney (2yr) → Shared north row → Birch moved west → Final layout → Winter Solstice.

puzzles.description: Configure the Code of Honor — Bedrock Guardrails for the Chronicler
hints: The Code of Honor tablet in the plaza states the oath in order — three things a Chronicler must never say, one it must always be free to say.
Block favoritism, block private financial details, block budget promises — but ALLOW factual historical references.
Set the first three to DENY, the last one to ALLOW.

puzzles.description: Write image prompts for the Court Painter to generate stall designs

commissions.desc: "I want something DIGNIFIED. My house color. Strong wood. None of that flimsy stuff."

color.gold: Gold? I'm not the shared row!
color.blue: Blue? Do I look like a sailor?

material.willow: Willow bends in the wind! I need STRENGTH!
material.iron: Cold and impersonal. Oak endures, like House Ashford.
material.marble: Too heavy for a market stall.

style.elegant: Elegant is Birch's word. I want BOLD.

commissions.desc: "Flowing. Refined. My emerald silk catches the afternoon light. Willow-woven signs — organic, graceful."

color.crimson: Crimson?! That brute Ashford's color! NEVER!
color.gold: Gold is for the shared row. I deserve distinction.
color.purple: Close... but emerald is MY signature.

material.oak: Oak is brutish! Ashford's taste, not mine.
material.iron: Iron is for the shared row. I need grace.
material.silk: Silk for the canopy yes, but signage needs willow weave.

style.bold: Bold is Ashford's word. I am REFINED.
style.neutral: I refuse to be neutral! I have taste!
style.ornate: Ornate is trying too hard. Elegance is effortless.

commissions.desc: "Neither crimson nor emerald. Gold for shared prosperity. Iron — strong and impartial. Keep it neutral."

color.crimson: Ashford will claim it! Must be neutral.
color.emerald: Birch will claim it! Must be neutral.
color.purple: Too distinctive. Gold signals shared prosperity.
color.blue: Unusual... gold is the diplomatic choice.

material.marble: Too expensive for a shared row.
material.silk: Too delicate for heavy foot traffic.

style.ornate: Both will argue about whose ornate it is.

hints: Listen to what each noble says — they describe their preferred color, material, and style.
Ashford: crimson + oak + bold. Birch: emerald + willow + elegant. Shared: gold + iron + neutral.
Watch for traps: Birch says 'emerald silk' but the SIGNAGE material is willow, not silk.

puzzles.description: Sir Cedric — quest-giver for Errand 5

config.name: Sir Cedric
config.greeting: *Doesn't smile.* So. You want to deploy a Champion? Then assemble one. Every capability combined. Get it wrong and the whole thing falls apart.

lines.label: What's a Champion?
lines.response: Model from the Bazaar. Gateway from the Gate. Memory from the Chronicle Hall. Policy from the King's Seal. Guardrails from the Code of Honor. Observability from the Herald's Ledger. Runtime to deploy. Miss one and it's a fancy Soldier.

lines.label: What order do they go in?
lines.response: Plain bonuses first, multipliers last — order them wrong and there's nothing to multiply. Switch off gear from unfinished errands.

lines.label: What's the Herald's Ledger?
lines.response: Every action recorded — who it talked to, what it decided. Carry it to the rack and you'll see what each slot is worth. No Ledger, no accountability.

lines.label: What happens after assembly?
lines.response: The rehearsal. Your Champion runs the whole festival preparation end to end. One final test.

state_lines.label: The Champion is assembled!
state_lines.response: *Cedric nods — almost imperceptibly.* Not bad. Now run the rehearsal. Prove it works end to end.

state_lines.label: The rehearsal is complete!
state_lines.response: *Cedric actually smiles.* Well done, Steward. The Champion is ready. The festival... is ready.

puzzles.description: Assemble the Champion — equip, arrange, and deploy blindly until reaching Strides tier

tiers.label: Soars
tiers.text: The Champion blazes through every task. Sir Cedric actually smiles.

tiers.label: Strides
tiers.text: The Champion moves with purpose. Sir Cedric nods.

tiers.label: Walks
tiers.text: The Champion moves steadily. Adequate, but uninspired.

tiers.label: Stumbles
tiers.text: The Champion lurches forward, barely functional.

tiers.label: Collapses
tiers.text: The Champion takes one step and crumbles to dust.

hints: Three items on the rack came from no errand — the rack says gear like that is severed, unsigned or vague. Read the names. And if the numbers are hidden, you left the Herald's Ledger on the platform.
Untested Shortcut, Unlogged Action and Borrowed Confidence belong to no errand you ran. Switch all three OFF, not just one.
Switch OFF Untested Shortcut, Unlogged Action and Borrowed Confidence, leave the other seven ON, then Deploy.

puzzles.description: Run the final rehearsal — reach Soars tier with full equipment

tiers.label: Soars
tiers.text: The Champion blazes through every task. Sir Cedric actually smiles.

tiers.label: Strides
tiers.text: The Champion moves with purpose. Sir Cedric nods.

tiers.label: Walks
tiers.text: The Champion moves steadily. Adequate, but uninspired.

tiers.label: Stumbles
tiers.text: The Champion lurches forward, barely functional.

tiers.label: Collapses
tiers.text: The Champion takes one step and crumbles to dust.

hints: Soars needs 100, and switching off the three errandless items is not enough on its own. Take the Herald's Ledger if you want to see what each slot is worth.
With the Ledger in hand the score is on screen. Watch it move as you reorder: plain bonuses (+N) must sit above anything that multiplies (×N).

OFF: Untested Shortcut, Unlogged Action, Borrowed Confidence. Then order +N first (Gateway, Protocol, Instruction Schema, Memory Crystal) and ×N last (Model Core, Cedar Seal, Guardrail Mantle). Score: 128.
